summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic systolic heart failure, and seizure disorder was admitted for epigastric abdominal pain and vomiting. Initial imaging showed gallbladder wall thickening concerning for cholecystitis, prompting treatment with antibiotics. A HIDA scan ruled out acute cholecystitis but revealed delayed tracer emptying, suggestive of sphincter of Oddi spasm. Symptoms improved with conservative management and anti-nausea medication. Elevated liver enzymes were noted but attributed to chronic changes; hepatitis workup was initiated. The patient remained afebrile, with resolution of symptoms, and was discharged home on unchanged medications with follow-up in gastroenterology.
